description: Composite EBSD figure characterising the microstructure of the cross-section near the fracture surface of a Fe-20Mn-6Al-0.6C-0.15Si low-density steel. (a) is an inverse-pole-figure (IPF) orientation map of the sample tested at -196 °C; (b) is the equivalent IPF map for the sample tested at RT. Both maps carry the same IPF colour-triangle legend (inset, top right, labelled 001, 101, 111) and a 200 µm scale bar (bottom left); a large black, unindexed region occupying the lower part of each map is the fracture/crack area, and in (a) the primary crack path cuts a zigzag trace across the mapped area. In (b) two white arrows label "Grain A" on either side of a crack. (c) is a line-scan misorientation profile: misorientation (°) on the vertical axis (0-7°) versus distance (µm) on the horizontal axis (0-40); red dashed vertical lines delimit the interval labelled "Crack", with "Grain A" printed on both sides. The trace fluctuates between 0 and just above the 3° gridline within the left Grain A region, drops to zero inside the crack band, and recovers to about 1° in the right Grain A region. Together the panels demonstrate that the regions flanking the crack are parts of one prior grain, i.e. transgranular fracture.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a colour IPF EBSD orientation map of the region near the fracture for the sample tested at -196 °C, with a 200 µm scale bar at bottom left and an IPF colour-triangle legend (001, 101, 111) inset at top right.

Panel (b) is a colour IPF EBSD orientation map of the region near the fracture for the sample tested at RT, using the same 001/101/111 IPF legend and 200 µm scale bar; two white arrows label the crack flank as 'Grain A'.
In both (a) and (b) large black (unindexed) areas mark the fracture/crack region, and the crack path in (a) has a zigzag geometry running across the lower part of the map.

Panel (c) plots misorientation in degrees (vertical axis, 0-7°, ticked every 1°) against distance in µm (horizontal axis, 0-40 µm, ticked every 5 µm), with red dashed vertical lines demarcating the interval labelled 'Crack' and 'Grain A' printed on both sides.

In panel (c) the misorientation trace oscillates between 0° and a value just above the 3° gridline over roughly 0-22 µm (left 'Grain A'), falls to a flat 0° inside the crack interval (about 23-37 µm), and rises again to about the 1° level beyond ~38 µm (right 'Grain A'); no numeric values are printed on the curve itself.
The caption states that (a) is the sample tested at -196 °C, (b) the sample tested at RT, and (c) the misorientation analysis for the region near fracture.
The citing text states that for both the -196 °C and RT samples the primary crack propagation paths at the fracture surface exhibit a zigzag shape, with most regions showing transgranular fracture.

The citing text states that the misorientation difference between the regions on both sides of the crack is less than 15°, implying the two regions were in the same grain before cracking, i.e. transgranular fracture (this threshold is asserted in the text, not printed on the panel).

The citing text states that secondary cracks are present in the sample tested at RT but not at -196 °C, and that they release stress concentration at primary-crack tips, contributing to better toughness and higher crack propagation energy at RT.

The citing text states that crack propagation causes severe plastic deformation near the primary cracks, producing a significant local orientation gradient adjacent to the cracks inside the grain interiors.

subfigures.description: Colour IPF EBSD orientation map of the cross-section near the fracture of the sample tested at -196 °C. 200 µm scale bar at bottom left; IPF triangle legend (001/101/111) inset at top right. A large black unindexed region occupies the lower-left part of the map, with a zigzag crack path separating it from the coloured grain structure.

Colour IPF EBSD orientation map of the cross-section near the fracture of the sample tested at RT, same colour legend (001/101/111) and 200 µm scale bar as (a). Two white arrows at the bottom right point to a crack with the label 'Grain A' on both sides; black unindexed crack region along the lower edge.

Line-scan misorientation profile: misorientation (°) (0-7, ticked every 1) versus distance (µm) (0-40, ticked every 5). Red dashed vertical lines delimit the 'Crack' interval; 'Grain A' is printed on the left and right sides. The profile oscillates between 0 and a little above 3° over roughly 0-22 µm, is flat at 0° from ~23 to ~37 µm (the crack), then rises again to ~1° beyond ~38 µm.

unreadable_items: Exact numeric values of the misorientation trace in panel (c) cannot be read (no data labels); only the 0-7° axis gridlines are available.
Grain boundary structure inside the black unindexed fracture regions of (a) and (b) is not resolvable.
